specFirst: This file was written BEFORE the code (PropostaAgentNewSolution.md §2.5). The code is validated against it: each step declares inputs/outputs/gate, and an automated test checks that the implementation matches this spec. Maintenance changes the spec FIRST, then the code.
description: Step-based pipeline with consistent checkpoints. Each step reads ONLY the frozen files from the previous step and writes ONLY its own files (zero canonical state in task payloads). Every checkpoint has 3 faces: machine artifact (JSON/defs.ts with versioned schema), human summary (md), and deterministic gate (code, no LLM). Phase 1 implements up to the 2nd human checkpoint (E1+E2); E3..E7 are declared as planned.
principles: Compiler-style pipeline, not a task tree: no passive containers. Fan-out uses the collab-messages parallel system (REVISED 2026-07-08 - the proposal's 'list iteration inside the step' is not possible: LLM calls only happen via prompt_ready, one per step run; the parallel system adds bounded concurrency, slot cleanup and good UX). Disk artifacts + the finalize repair round keep the determinism the proposal wanted.

Fail early: repair means rerun step N with the gate error in context (1 retry); if it persists, show a visible checkpoint failure with a readable partial artifact. No FREE-FORM LLM critic (REVISED 2026-08-02, improveJourneys T4): a TYPED JUDGE is allowed, and only under all four bounds — (1) it emits findings against a CLOSED rubric of codes declared in a versioned schema, and severity is assigned by the code in host code, never by the model; (2) it NEVER writes an artifact — at most it feeds findings into the step's standard retryContext channel, so the single write path is untouched; (3) it is bounded by construction: at most 2 judge calls and at most 1 regeneration per step run, and a judge that keeps disagreeing does not block — the run proceeds carrying the findings; (4) it is never the authority: the deterministic gate and the human checkpoint decide. A finding the host cannot act on (invented code, unknown id, a field the artifact version does not have) is discarded with a reason in the trace. A judge that cannot run (no payload, unreadable output) is skipped, never a failure.
Step is the maintenance unit: 1 folder per step (agent, prompt.md, schema, gate, test, fixture, readme, CHANGELOG). helpers/ is minimal and policy-frozen (it does not know step-specific logic).
System that builds systems: local examples or point fixes embedded in prompts/gates are forbidden; fixes generalize or they do not enter.
No console: everything goes to trace; errors appear objectively in the task.

UI: the step list is a tree ONLY for presentation (visual grouping derived from this flow.json, with no orchestration/dependency semantics). Step strings are translated to the user's language, as in v2.
CLI-like: commands such as /rebuild e2 rerun a step while skipping already completed ones; dirty propagation (inputsHash) prevents skipping steps when upstream changed.

conventions.module: {module} = module name proposed in E1 and normalized by the E1 gate (first disk write; no temporary folder).
conventions.pipelineState: l4/{module}/pipeline/pipeline.json = pipeline state: per step {status: pending|running|gate_failed|approved, inputsHash, artifactVersion, approvedAt, approvedBy: auto|human}. The runner is dumb: it reads pipeline.json and runs the next non-approved step. Resume means looking at the last approved gate.
conventions.artifacts: Phase artifacts in l4/{module}/pipeline/e{N}-*.{json,md}. Final artifacts (from E3 onward) use the SAME paths/formats as v2 (l4/{module}/ontology, l4/actors, l4/rules, l4/workflows, l4/operations, l4/{module}/journeys, l5/{module}) so Stage 2/3 do not change.
conventions.schemas: Versioned schemas/e{N}-*.schema.json files ($id with version). Schema and gate only change with a version bump + fixture update. Loosening a gate to pass a fix = upstream bug.
conventions.gates: 1 gate = 1 file = 1 .test.ts, inside the step folder. The gate validates schema + semantic invariants. Warnings do not block; errors block and trigger 1 retry with the error in context. IMPORTANT (2026-07-08, refined 2026-07-29): a gate-failed run with a retry in flight must NOT go 'failed' - update-status 'failed' marks the whole task as failed (collab-messages updateStepStatus) and, because e1/e2 downstream depends on the RUN planId (checkpoint-journeys dependsOn e2-journeys; e2 dependsOn e1-draft - no eN-done anchor there), the recovered retry could never unlock it (run04 deadlock: task stuck 'in progress' forever). Two sanctioned recovery shapes: (a) PARK - e1-draft/e2-journeys park the original step as waiting_human_input and the retry carries originStepId/originParentStepId; on success it completes the parked step ('recovered by gate retry') which unlocks downstream, on exhaustion it FAILS the parked step (task fails once, with the reason, exactly when the error message appears) and completes itself with trace; (b) COMPLETE-WITH-TRACE - e6 completes the failed run because its downstream (detail phase) is only added by the success path, so early completion unlocks nothing. Analysis: todo/collabMessages/bugStatus.md.
conventions.dirtyPropagation: Each step writes the hash of consumed inputs to pipeline.json. If an approved upstream artifact changes (for example, the E2 adjustment loop), downstream steps become dirty and runner/CLI refuses skip.
conventions.versioning: E2 adjustment-loop iterations generate e2-journeys.v{K}.json; 'approve' freezes the current version as e2-journeys.json and records the decision (source for the designContext in E3).
conventions.singleWritePath: Widgets NEVER write artifacts directly: every change (edit or adjustment prompt) passes through the adjustment agent + gate before being presented again.
conventions.rootPlan: agentNewSolution returns userLanguage, validPrompt/invalidReason, localized step titles, uiLabels for checkpoint widgets, and clarification 1 questions.
conventions.resume: An empty '@@newSolution' (the runtime strips the mention) resumes the first module whose Phase 1 is incomplete instead of starting a new one, so the user does not repeat the clarification. beforePromptImplicit scans l4/{module}/pipeline/pipeline.json; a step counts as done when approved OR its lastGate.ok is true. Phase 1 resume re-enters at e2-journeys or the journeys checkpoint; phase-2 resume (2026-07-08) re-enters at the next unapproved/dirty phase-2 step (pipeline.json order) rebuilding the chain from that step on - the first rebuilt step runs immediately and the rest keep their eN-done anchor dependencies. A non-empty prompt always starts a new module.
conventions.doneAnchors: Every phase-2 step eN publishes a completed 'result' step with planId 'eN-done' when (and only when) its gate passes. Downstream steps dependsOn ['eN-done'], never on the agent step planId: retries and adjustment runs have dynamic planIds, and unlockWaitingDependencySteps only unlocks on a COMPLETED step per planId, so the anchor is the stable contract regardless of which run succeeded.
conventions.itemChains: REVISED 2026-07-08 (was: sequential chains). Fan-out (E3 entities, E5 workflows/operations) uses the collab-messages PARALLEL system (5 slots, slot reuse, finished children deleted): the plan/classification step hosts the fan-out under itself (compact selector args 'entity:X'/'workflow:X'/'operation:X'), so its completion waits for the fan-out and anchors the next step. Fan-out children NEVER return 'failed' (a failed child fails the parent/task) and never add steps; on gate failure they complete-with-trace. A no-LLM finalize step ('e3-finalize'/'e5-finalize', with 'e5-operations-phase' as the workflows-to-operations barrier) verifies every defs file on disk, runs ONE sequential repair round for missing items, then writes the summary .md, approves the pipeline step and emits the 'eN-done' anchor. Completed runs pass cleaner 'input_output' so LLM payloads leave the task record (DynamoDB 400KB).
conventions.designContextPlacement: DEVIATION from PropostaAgentNewSolution §3-E3 (designContext as an ontology item): agentChangeBackend treats EVERY file under l4/{module}/ontology/ as a data entity (cbShared.readBackendScan) and would fold a DesignContext pseudo-entity into aggregate derivation. The design context therefore lives where Stage 2/3 already read it: module.defs.ts designContext (assembled in E7 from e1-draft + e2 decisions + audit), plus the pipeline artifacts which remain on disk.
conventions.consumerContract: Verified against agentChangeFrontend/helpers/.ts and agentChangeBackend/helpers/.ts (2026-07-07): consumers require ontology entity files (entityId,title,kind,ownership,fields,statusEnum,lifecycleStates,eventPolicy), module.defs.ts (module block, designContext.userLanguage, ontology.entities index, relationships), workflows (workflowId,pageId,title,actors,operationIds,entities,rulesApplied,story,capabilities), operations (operationId,commandName,pageId,bffName,entity,kind,reads,writes,accessPattern{kind,keyField Entity.field,pagination,output},inputs{inputId,fieldRef,required,source},contextResolution,rulesApplied,story,capability), journeys defs (workspaces{workspaceId,title,actor,kind,entity,workflowId,operationIds,purpose}, navigationEdges advisory — RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-02: this describes the LEGACY journeys-nested shape; the per-journey l4/{module}/journeys/{journeyId}.defs.ts files carry no `workspaces` key, so cfeCreateShared parses them to an empty entry that the standalone workspaces immediately supersede. Their narrative/operationIds/workspaceId shape is therefore free to improve without touching Stage 2/3), and l5 todoFrontend/todoBackend ({layer,moduleName,owners{ownerType,ownerId,status:'toCreate'}} - the ONLY generation-status source; inline statusFrontend/statusBackend are legacy). bffName = {module}.{pageId}.{commandName}; pageId = owning workflowId (else operationId); commandName = operationId - all attached deterministically, never by the LLM. l4/actors, l4/rules and l5/process.defs.ts are contract/documentation artifacts (not machine-read by Stage 2/3).
conventions.i18n: No hard-coded language; step strings, human summaries, and checkpoint uiLabels are generated in the user's language (userLanguage captured in E1).

folderLayout.agentNewSolution.ts: root: receives the prompt, registers the task, builds the visual step tree, delegates to the runner
folderLayout.skills/: platform.md (baseline: what NOT to model) + maintenance.md (mandatory LLM adjustment protocol)
folderLayout.helpers/: nsFs.ts (read/write/path hardening), nsIds.ts (id normalization), nsGate.ts (gate runner + retry), nsPipeline.ts (pipeline.json, inputsHash, dirty), nsTrace.ts
folderLayout.schemas/: Versioned JSON Schemas for artifacts between steps
folderLayout.steps/e1-draft/: readme.md, agentNsDraft.ts, prompt.md, gate.ts, gate.test.ts, fixture/
folderLayout.steps/e2-journeys/: readme.md, agentNsJourneys.ts, prompt.md, gate.ts, gate.test.ts, fixture/, promptJudge.md + judge.ts/.test.ts + e2JudgeLive.test.ts (the typed judge), widgetNsJourneys.ts/.less and widgetNsJourneysLogic.ts
folderLayout.widgetNsJourneys.ts/.less: human checkpoint 2 (graphical journeys + features/priorities + adjustment prompt)

treeOverview: phase-understanding (visual): e1-clarification -> e1-clarification-answer -> e1-draft (auto-approved, NO human checkpoint)
phase-business (visual): e2-journeys -> checkpoint-journeys (2nd and last human interaction; adjustment loop)

steps.goal: 1st human interaction. The agent container emits a runtime clarification payload, matching agentNewSolution2Requirements. Validate the prompt as early as possible: if invalid/insufficient (admission gate: empty, out of scope, no system intent), return an objective error + this clarification. Minimal opening questions; no architecture.
Task result created after the user submits clarification 1. This plan id is the dependency that unlocks e1-draft; e1-draft must not be manually moved to pending.

Additional human clarification opened only when the E1 gate finds a blocking question. The partial e1-draft.json/.md remains saved, pipeline.json keeps e1-draft as gate_failed, and the answer reruns E1 with blockingAnswers and previousModuleName.
Analyze the prompt and deliver the draft (understanding contract, 1 page): proposed module, problem, presumed actors, scope in/out, classified open questions, language.

checks: valid e1-draft schema
normalized and non-colliding module name
every open question is classified (blocking | assumed with default)
userLanguage is present
gate.onBlockingDoubt: opens an additional clarification instead of continuing

steps.goal: REMOVED (2026-07-06). Per PropostaAgentNewSolution §8 there are only TWO human interactions (clarification and journeys), so E1 is NOT a human checkpoint. E1 auto-approves on a green gate (approveNsStep 'auto') and the pipeline goes straight to E2. The e1-draft.md remains on disk as the understanding contract / E2 input. widgetNsDraft.* stays in the repo but is not wired.

Analyze/enrich user journeys and generate the feature catalog - WITHOUT ontology. Journeys by actor (steps with intent and result, no layout/page) + features with now/soon/later/never priority. Absorbs v2 discover-scope + recommend + decisions into ONE consistent delivery.

checks: valid e2-journeys schema
every feature is referenced by at least one journey step
every actor has at least one journey
priorities are complete (now/soon/later/never)
ids are normalized and unique
every e1 actor is present (removed actors require an explicit recorded decision)

prerequisite (schema v2, 2026-08-02): where the actor comes from. A journey with no prerequisite is an ENTRY journey (starts cold on the actor's landing) — valid. kind 'journey' must name a journey that exists, must not be the journey itself, and must declare non-empty carries (prerequisite_journey_missing / _unknown_journey / _self_reference / _carries_empty, all ERROR); kind external/schedule must not reference a journey (prerequisite_journey_ref_unexpected); the graph of 'comes from' edges must terminate (prerequisite_cycle). A prerequisite whose journey belongs to ANOTHER actor is a handoff: a FACT, exposed by describeNsE2Prerequisites to the widget and the checkpoint markdown (Journey Entry Points), never a gate issue the human would dismiss on every run. The v1 free-text `trigger` is still read for compatibility and never produced. Whether a journey SHOULD have declared a prerequisite is semantic and belongs to the e2 judge, not to this gate

steps.goal: TYPED JUDGE (2026-08-02, improveJourneys T4). Added by e2-journeys on a GREEN gate, before the human checkpoint — the artifact is small, the regeneration is a single step and the human has not looked yet. One call against the closed rubric of steps/e2-journeys/promptJudge.md: J1 journey.step.locateMissing (acts on an existing record the narrative never reaches), J2 journey.prerequisite.missing/.invalid (continues another journey without declaring what arrives — only on schema v2+), J3 journey.actor.stepMismatch (a step its actor cannot perform), J4 entity.noReadSurface (a record commanded but never shown, module-wide), J5 journey.outcome.unobservable. J1/J2/J3 are ERRORS, J4/J5 WARNINGS — assigned by code, never by the model. It is the judge that opens the checkpoint afterwards. SKIPPED in /fast mode (the checkpoint auto-approves there, so a review plus a regeneration would only cost time).
input: l4/{module}/pipeline/e2-journeys.json (narrative + actors only; the feature catalog is not sent)

savedArtifact: the Journey Review section appended to e2-journeys.md

checks: a finding whose code is not in the rubric is discarded
a finding naming a journey that does not exist is discarded
a finding with no journeyId is discarded unless its code is the module-wide entity.noReadSurface
a stepId that does not resolve is dropped from the finding, which is kept
duplicates by code+journey+subject are discarded
prerequisite findings are discarded on an artifact older than the schema version that introduced the field
every discard is recorded with a reason (a silent drop must never read as a clean review)

ERROR findings on the FIRST review of a non-adjustment run trigger exactly ONE e2 regeneration through the standard retryContext; on the second review, or over a version the human just asked for, findings are annotated and the run proceeds

steps.goal: 2nd human interaction - the most important business checkpoint. The agent emits a clarification payload owned by this step; beforeClarificationStep renders widgetNsJourneys. The widget shows journeys by actor, feature priorities, editable notes/rules, and an adjustment prompt. Loop: user request -> a new dynamic e2-journeys adjustment step applies it -> gate -> new version v{K} presented again. Approval freezes the current version.

output.result: clarification UI submitted by the user; approval creates checkpoint-journeys-answer, adjustment creates a new e2-journeys run

steps.notes: singleWritePath: the widget never writes artifacts directly. All approvals/adjustments are stored as task steps and in e2-journeys-audit.json. Strong implementation pattern (2026-07-06): custom checkpoint UI is a clarification emitted in the owning agent interaction payload, as documented in skills/collab_messages.md and used by agentNewSolution2Requirements. Dynamic adjustment steps reuse agentNsJourneys instead of a separate agent file, keeping generation/gate/write behavior in one maintenance unit.

steps.goal: Task result created only when the user approves the E2 journeys checkpoint. This is the dependency that unlocks E3; adjustment requests intentionally do not create this result.

savedArtifact: pipeline.json with e2-journeys and checkpoint-journeys approvedBy=human

steps.goal: Ontology plan + per-entity generation. The plan call reads e2-journeys.json (+ e1-draft.json) and produces e3-model.json: the module block (title/purpose/businessDomain/languages/visualStyle), a slim entity index (entityId PascalCase, title, description, kind core|supporting|event|metric|mdm, ownership, statusEnum/lifecycleStates, sourceRefs to journeys/features/businessRules) and relationships. Then a sequential item chain generates one FULL entity per file (fields with types uuid|string|text|number|money|boolean|date|datetime|<EntityId>, enums, audit fields, statusEnum aligned with journey business rules).

output.result: entity model plan, then one canonical entity per file

checks: valid e3-model schema
PascalCase unique entity ids; anti Uc*/usecase/verb guard
relationships resolve to declared entities
every non-never E2 feature is covered by >=1 entity sourceRef (warning)

per entity: valid e3-entity schema, unique camelCase fieldIds, valid field types (<EntityId> refs resolve), enum fields carry enum values, statusEnum consistent with lifecycleStates, id + createdAt/updatedAt audit fields present

steps.goal: Single call: actor roster (roleScope '{module}:{actorId}'), the consolidated rule set (E2 per-journey businessRules are the primary source - every journey rule maps to a ruleId or is explicitly absorbed) and external references (MDM/horizontals/plugins/agents) that E7 writes into module.defs.ts approvedArtifacts.

checks: valid e4 schema
every E2 actor is in the roster (extra supporting actors allowed)
roleScope format {module}:{actorId}
unique camelCase ruleIds
every rule appliesTo resolves to an E3 entity
every E2 journey businessRule maps to a ruleId (unmapped = warning)

steps.goal: Classification call first: e5-classification.json maps every non-never E2 feature to workflows (stateful, with owned operationIds) and standalone operations, declaring actor/entity/kind per item. Then a sequential item chain: one LLM call per workflow (states/transitions aligned with the primary entity lifecycle, embedded story) and per operation (reads/writes, accessPattern with keyField 'Entity.field', inputs with declared sources, contextResolution, acceptanceAssertions derived from journey step results). pageId/commandName/bffName/capability are attached deterministically after each call - never by the LLM.

output.result: classification, then one behavior per file

checks: valid schemas (classification, workflow, operation)
every non-never E2 feature realized by >=1 workflow/operation
every workflow has non-empty operationIds and every referenced operation is classified
workflow states align with the primary entity statusEnum/lifecycleStates
transitions reference declared states and classified operations
operation kind in create|update|delete|query|view
reads/writes/entity resolve to E3 entities
accessPattern.keyField is 'Entity.field' with a real field
inputs sources valid; required inputs have inputId+fieldRef+source
bffName == {module}.{pageId}.{commandName} (deterministic attach re-checked)
every entity with standalone write operations has a managedEntities entry (deletionPolicy delete|inactivate|immutable)
policy delete requires a delete operation; inactivate requires a statusEnum inactivationState + update operation; immutable requires a reason and forbids delete
self-transitions (from == to) are a workflow gate error
finalize demotes workflow-listed operations without a real transition (create trigger exempt) and re-validates managedEntities post-demotion
managedEntities requirement scoped by E3 entity kind (mdm = error; core with statusEnum = warning)

steps.goal: P7 TWO-PHASE (newSolution_14): phase 1 'e6-journey-map' is a single LIGHT call producing the permanent SITE MAP (l4/{module}/siteMap.defs.ts — workspaces id/title/actors/kind/entity/workflowId/operationIds/purpose + landings + advisory edges; absorbs the old navigation.defs.ts). Phase 2 'e6-detail' is a parallel_dynamic fan-out (1 call per workspace) producing l4/{module}/workspaces/{workspaceId}.defs.ts (sections/organisms/bffCalls + sliceHash for incremental re-runs). 'e6-finalize' (no LLM) reassembles map+details and runs the authoritative validateE6Invariants + a repair round, then emits e6-done.
input: operation defs summaries (light for phase 1; full projection vocab per-workspace for phase 2)

checks: valid e6 schema
every operation appears in >=1 workspace
workspace workflowId/operationIds/actor/entity resolve
unique workspaceIds
every actor with now-priority behaviors has a landing (warning)
edges reference existing pageIds (warning)
workspace kind derived deterministically from the classification (workflow-owned ops -> workflow; standalone create+update on the entity -> entityManagement; else operation)
entityManagement workspaces never declare workflowId
presentation.categoryRef (and each alternate) exists in the categoryList.json catalog handed in through the gate context (ERROR); catalog integrity = duplicate ids / dangling parentCategory (ERROR)

presentation styleRef resolves to a _102040_ template folder, confidence < 6, missing presentation and the coarse category-vs-shape findings are WARNINGS (a retry cannot fix run configuration; a low score is signal for a new category)
every presentation check naming a category id no-ops when that id leaves the catalog (categoryList.json is the single source of truth; an unreachable catalog warns once and skips)

a required id input on a command must resolve INSIDE the workspace: source selection -> sourceRef is a query bffId of this workspace, derived -> sourceRef starts at a local bffCall, pageInput/actorSession need no ref; missing source or userDecision on an id is an ERROR (bff.input.idSourceMissing) whose message names both ways out

ANY required input (query calls and non-id names included) must declare a source: no source at all is an ERROR (bff.input.sourceMissing) — the command-only id rule above let a required id on a query through e6 AND e7 with zero findings

a required id with source pageInput needs a PROVIDER, verified over the WHOLE map at finalize (T5, the hole gate.test.ts used to assert was empty): a navigation into this workspace whose `from` page displays that field in a query output, between pages that share an actor (an edge across disjoint actors is a HANDOFF, not navigation) and never the id of the record the edge's own operation CREATES; OR a journey declaring the actor arrives here with that record (prerequisite.carries from the human-approved e2, resolved to an entity and matched by the <entity>Id convention). Neither = ERROR bff.input.pageInputUnfed naming both ways out. When the convention cannot decide (the id name resolves to no declared entity, or the declared carries resolve to none) it degrades to WARNING bff.input.pageInputUnverified — inventing an error over a naming convention would burn the run's single repair round. The check does NOT force query co-location (P2 stays out): a command-only page is fine as long as something feeds its ids

a workspace that is an actor's LANDING is opened cold: a required input with source pageInput is an ERROR (landing.requiresPageInput) and a selection/derived that does not resolve inside the page is an ERROR (landing.input.unresolved). The message names the way out the model can still act on: host a query that resolves the record from the actor's own context (the current/open one) and feed the input from it, or take it from the session. The landing of the workspace under detail is passed into the detail-phase gate and stated in the detail prompt, so the retry can fix it while the page is being designed

P2 co-location (2026-08-03, phase 1, deterministic): a required id input of an operation this workspace hosts, whose name resolves to a DECLARED entity, gets that entity's listing operation added to the workspace — but ONLY when nothing else can feed it (the page already reads the entity, a journey prerequisite carries it, or a navigation from a same-actor page that displays it and does not go there to CREATE it). Reusing one operation in several workspaces is the BFF pattern, not a compromise: one usecase, several BFF calls, verified end to end on 03/08 (gen-usecase is 1 per operation, controllers are per workspace with prefixed handlers, every coverage check is >= 1). A co-located READ never changes the workspace kind (workflow short-circuits on hasWorkflowOp; entityManagement is preserved by the foreignReadOnly tolerance)

P2 picker marking (finalize, stamped by CODE never the LLM): a query bffCall whose operations are all of ANOTHER entity than the workspace AND that a `selection` input points at gets `usage: "picker"` — it exists to fill a field. A query over the page's OWN entity is the master-detail SURFACE and is never stamped. Gate: a picker used as a section primarySurface is an ERROR (bff.picker.asPrimarySurface); a picker no input selects from is a WARNING (bff.picker.unreferenced). The enum has ONE value on purpose — a second is added when a second real case exists

journeys (derived at finalize, never the LLM's): operationIds = per STEP the operations covering ALL of the step's featureRefs (partial matches only when nothing covers the whole step), of the journey's own actor, narrowed to the entity the journey WRITES to (ties: most operations, then id order) without leaving any step unserved; the anchor workspaceId = the workspace that includes the actor and hosts the most of those operations, ties broken by the page hosting the journey's writes, then by the actor's landing. Gate: operationIds resolve (ERROR), workspaceId resolves (ERROR), the anchor includes the journey's actor (ERROR journey.anchor.actorMismatch), an operation classified for another actor is a WARNING (journey.operation.foreignActor), an operation exercised by no journey is a WARNING (expected to be non-zero now that journeys no longer sweep every operation: it names the operations the e2 has no journey about)

steps.goal: Deterministic (no LLM) global recheck + closing. Reads ONLY saved files: cross-consistency checks (v2 code style: workflow.operation.unknown, entity.ref.unknown, capability coverage, journey workspace coverage, bff naming) written to behavior-health-report.json (errors block). Then assembles module.defs.ts (module block from e3-model, designContext from e1-draft + e2 decisions/audit, ontology index from entity files, relationships, approvedArtifacts from e4 refs), seeds l5 todoFrontend/todoBackend (one owner per workflow/operation, status toCreate) and l5 process.defs.ts, and writes the reopenable e7-validation.md summary.
input: all saved l4 artifacts (files only, never payload)

checks: health report has zero errors (warnings do not block)
module.defs.ts index matches the ontology files on disk
todo owners exactly match generated workflows+operations

template-readiness lint (steps/e7-validation/templateLint.ts): every classified workspace is checked against its category minimumRequired in categoryList.json — ok / repaired (FORM only: a list output lifted into a paginated envelope) / downgraded to an alternate the contract satisfies / templateReady:false / skipped when the category has no minimumRequired. ALL WARNINGS: a page on the generic fallback is not a broken module

universal (any category): a REQUIRED id input on a command with no source (or source userDecision) is a finding here — the ERROR that forces the fix lives at e6 (bff.input.idSourceMissing), where the model can still add the picker query or declare pageInput; e7 is the net
ordering: the lint runs BEFORE emitNsBffContracts (the wire contracts derive from the same workspaces) and rewrites repaired workspaces whole, preserving sliceHash
T6: l4/{module}/trace/template-readiness.json per run + the coverage table appended to pipeline/e7-validation.md

commands: /rebuild e{N} (reruns the step; refuses if upstream is dirty)
/replay e{N} fixture={name} (golden run: runs the step on the fixture and performs a structural invariant diff)

PROMPT FLAGS (parsed from the initial prompt, stripped from it, carried in longMemory): /fast auto-accepts both human clarifications; /rebuild cleans the module l4+l5 before regenerating; /l4only (2026-08-03) stops after the spec — e7 writes every l4/l5 artifact as always but does NOT start the @@changeFrontend/@@changeBackend follow-up tasks, for when the SPEC is what is being iterated on

handoffArtifacts.finalProduces: identical to agentNewSolution2 (Stage 2/3 do not change)
